summary: This is a closed GitHub issue (#367) in the ros-infrastructure/rosdep repository titled "rosdep fails if pip is not installed", opened by mitchellwills on Jan 6, 2015. The reporter saw rosdep throw an internal error with "Bad installer [pip]" when pip was missing, and suggested installing pip implicitly. Maintainer wjwwood explained that asserting pip is available is intended when a pip key is needed, and closed the issue; later commenters in 2017-2018 reported the same error, and a collaborator suggested the fix is to install pip and to make the error message clearer.
one_line: GitHub issue #367 in the rosdep project reporting that rosdep raises an internal error when pip is not installed, closed as intended behavior.
key_facts: GitHub issue #367 in the ros-infrastructure/rosdep repository is titled "rosdep fails if pip is not installed".
The issue was opened by user mitchellwills on Jan 6, 2015 and had 15 comments.
mitchellwills reported the problem on hydro 12.04 and indigo 13.10.
The error output was "Bad installer [pip]: [Errno 2] No such file or directory" under rosdep version 0.11.0.
mitchellwills ran the command rosdep install -i --from-paths src in the root of a catkin workspace.
A package in the src directory depended on a rosdep key that resolved to a pip package.
wjwwood, a contributor, said that when a pip key is needed rosdep will assert that pip is available, which is intended behavior, and closed the issue on Jan 6, 2015.
wjwwood wrote that rosdep will except if --simulate is used, but not when nothing in the workspace depends on a key resolving to pip.
wjwwood said the top part of the error output is attached to all exceptions and that exception handling should be changed to be more palatable.
mitchellwills said the error should print bad installer without the internal error message, since it is not really an internal error.
On Dec 28, 2017, bryan-bisonai reported the same error with rosdep version 0.11.8 using the kinetic rosdistro.
On Apr 4, 2018, aniroodh-ravikumar reported that the error persisted after pip was installed, with rosdep version 0.12.2, and that pip --version failed with a missing /usr/local/bin/pip.
aniroodh-ravikumar's python was located at /opt/local/bin/python, running Python 2.7.14.
NikolausDemmel, a collaborator, said that pip must be runnable from the shell and suggested python -m pip install --force-reinstall -U pip.
wjwwood said /opt/local/bin is probably macports, which none of the maintainers use regularly.
